source.title: Comparing Latent Concept Formation in State Space Models and Transformers via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Rithin Nagaraj; Rupa Laalasa Oruganti; Prerna Subhashchandra Kunder; Ashwini M. Joshi

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text, including the conclusion and references, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports SAE-feature alignment and selected feature examples, but it does not measure neuron-pole job shares or test any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study analyzes SAE features and their cross-model co-activation, not the share of neurons with one or more human-interpretable jobs or the accuracy of neuron explanations on held-out activations. Its results therefore do not test the listed versions. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study compares SAE features (dictionary directions) between Mamba-130m and Pythia-70m-deduped using cross-model Jaccard co-activation. It does not measure how many neurons or neuron poles have one, two or unknown jobs. It does not test neuron explanations on held-out activations, does not build neuron-based attribution graphs, and does not examine InceptionV1. Its use of the word 'neurons' for SAE features does not make it a neuron audit. It neither tests nor relies on the essay's claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Mamba and Pythia SAE feature spaces are nearly fully aligned (99.98%), that architecture has negligible impact on core semantic representations, and that divergence is confined to structural and syntactic margins. There, Mamba may show landmark features and 'concept cramming'. They call the polysemanticity result hypothesis-generating and acknowledge the dictionary-size confound.
record.recipe_differences: Uses sparse autoencoders and maximum binary co-activation Jaccard similarity between Mamba and Pythia features; it does not use the neuron-pole audit or held-out explanation tests described by the claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-architecture maximum-Jaccard alignment of SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the study's dictionaries, layers, corpus and empirically chosen thresholds, 12,285 of 12,288 Mamba-130m SAE features have a Pythia-70m-deduped SAE feature with Jaccard above 0.35 (observed range 0.234–0.412).

fits_no_version.finding: Qualitative examples of low-alignment SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In one selected twin pair, a Mamba SAE feature fires on several unrelated syntactic contexts, while its Pythia twin fires narrowly on table timestamps. The authors call this hypothesis-generating and note a confound from unequal SAE expansion factors (16 vs 64).

record.problems: The study notes unequal SAE dictionary expansion factors (16 for Mamba and 64 for Pythia), which may affect alignment and polysemanticity. It acknowledges that its Jaccard category thresholds are empirically chosen and lack a null-distribution baseline. The polysemanticity argument relies on one qualitative Twin pair and is described by the authors as hypothesis-generating. The comparison covers only two models and one corpus and layer per model.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible study results were left out. The paper's cited findings from other work were excluded.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and no job-share estimates.
No neuron-job shares in any model. It reports only SAE-feature alignment in two small models (130m, 70m); no MoE models and no scale range.
No vision models, no InceptionV1, and no cat-and-car neuron analysis.

No interpretable-neuron shares compared across tools, architectures or regularization. Its claim that Mamba's recurrent bottleneck drives polysemanticity concerns SAE features from one qualitative pair.
No attribution graphs and no comparison with a replacement model.
No tests of explanations against held-out activations. Feature descriptions rest on top activating snippets only.

record.verdict_notes: The paper calls SAE features 'neurons', for example 'polysemantic junk drawer neurons'. This terminology should not be read as evidence on neuron-level interpretability shares. It also does not cite either original source.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B or estimate the share of neuron poles with one, two, or unknown jobs.
Compares SAE-feature alignment for Mamba-130m and Pythia-70m-deduped; it does not measure neuron-job shares across models, dense and MoE systems, or parameter scales up to trillions.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car example.
Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares across architectures, tools, or regularization settings.
Does not test neuron-based attribution graphs or compare them with a replacement model.
Does not test explanations against activations outside the examples used to write them.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Mamba-130m
rows.operation_detail: Compared each Mamba SAE feature's binary co-activation pattern with Pythia features and recorded its maximum Jaccard similarity.

conditions.value: 12,288 Mamba features compared with 32,768 Pythia features
Aligned J > 0.35; Grey Matter J in [0.28, 0.35]; Alien/Structural J < 0.25

rows.measure: Distribution of maximum cross-model Jaccard similarities for Mamba SAE features
rows.value: 99.98% (12,285) were Aligned (J > 0.35); 2 features (0.02%) were Grey Matter (J in [0.28, 0.35]); 1 feature (0.01%) was Alien/Structural (J < 0.25). Global minimum Jaccard similarity was 0.2343 and maximum was 0.4116.
rows.note: This is a feature-level alignment distribution, not a measurement of interpretable neuron-job shares.
rows.check: The values match the text, but the paper is internally inconsistent. Its percentages (99.98% + 0.02% + 0.01%) sum to over 100%. Section IV.B calls the diverging fraction 0.03%, while elsewhere it says 0.02%. The thresholds leave the buffer zone [0.25, 0.28) unassigned, and there is no null baseline. This is cross-model SAE-feature alignment, not interpretability of neurons.

rows.measure: Feature activation contexts and stated function
rows.value: Reported to fire with high magnitude (Strength: 4.19) exclusively on External LINKS headers at the end of Wikipedia articles; described as a document-terminating trigger.
rows.note: The authors describe this SAE feature as monosemantic; this is not an audit of neuron poles.
rows.check: A selected SAE-feature example, not a neuron audit. Its J = 0.3415 places it in the Grey Matter band.

rows.subject: Mamba-130m

rows.measure: Feature activation contexts and stated function
rows.value: Reported to trigger with Strength 6.96 specifically on URL path separators.
rows.note: The paper characterizes this as a structural landmark; it does not report a neuron-job share.

rows.subject: Mamba-130m
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively inspected activating contexts for Mamba SAE Feature 4454 in a Twin Test.
rows.value: Reported to fire on the same table timestamps as its Pythia twin and also on URL slashes (Strength: 6.39), K-12 grade hyphens (4.58), and capitalized foreign-language substrings (4.18).
rows.note: The authors call this SAE feature polysemantic. The qualitative case study does not quantify neuron-job shares or explanation accuracy.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m-deduped
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively inspected activating contexts for Pythia SAE Feature 4309 as the Twin Test comparator.
rows.value: Described as a monosemantic trigger for newline spacing immediately following a timestamp in Wikipedia tables; Table I lists three timestamp contexts with strengths 4.87, 4.83, and 4.79.
rows.note: This is one qualitative SAE-feature comparison, not a measurement of neuron-job shares.

relation.reason: It discusses polysemantic and monosemantic SAE features but does not test the claim.

tranche.reason: SAE-feature Jaccard alignment across architectures; no neuron-job shares or held-out explanation tests.

source_check.notes: The text calls SAE features "neurons" (abstract; "dedicated neurons" in IV.B). Its Mamba SAE is custom-trained with expansion factor 16, against the pretrained Pythia SAE's factor 64. Category percentages are inconsistent: 99.98+0.02+0.01 is over 100%, and IV.B says 0.03%. The polysemanticity finding comes from one twin pair, and the authors call it hypothesis-generating.
